Definition: to commit adultery; figuratively, to apostatize
BiblicalUsage: Na'aph means to commit adultery, and the Bible uses it for the act and for the unfaithfulness it pictures. The command is plain in Exodus 20:14, and the penalty is stated in Leviticus 20:10. Proverbs 6:32 says the adulterer destroys his own soul, and in Jeremiah 3:8 the Lord says backsliding Israel committed adultery and was put away.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe adultery is never only about a body, because God calls His own people adulterers when they chase other gods. The marriage bed and the covenant with God break in the same place: a promise kept only while it is easy. I hold that keeping faith in both is what a faithful life is.
